## Project Overview

This project analyzes customer churn using statistical modeling techniques. Completed as a final project for the Marketing Science course at Hitotsubashi University, the analysis aims to identify key risk factors and predict customer retention.

## Methodology
This analysis employs a two-step statistical approach to understand and predict customer churn.

### 1. Dimension Reduction (Factor Analysis)

First, **Factor Analysis** was applied to survey data to condense multiple customer satisfaction variables into interpretable latent factors, reducing dimensionality and avoiding multicollinearity.

### 2. Churn Prediction (Survival Analysis)

Using the extracted factors as covariates, a Cox Proportional Hazards Model was fitted to estimate the hazard ratios. This allows for the quantification of how each satisfaction factor impacts the probability of customer churn over time.
